rulings.docket_item: PAIRED, one seam raised from both sides: close P10-012 at Jer.29.19 and open P10-013 at Jer.29.20 in place of the current 29:20|29:21 seam - adopt for both or decline for both.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived from the staged bytes; the seam is weighed ONCE for both rows. oshb:Jer.29.20 opens וְאַתֶּ֖ם שִׁמְע֣וּ דְבַר יְהוָ֑ה כָּל הַ֨גּוֹלָ֔ה (byte) - a plural discourse-frame imperative carrying a vocative that names its own audience. Discourse-frame imperatives are a ruled tier-1 internal seam class, and the class is functional rather than needle-bound: its two named exemplars, the declare-and-blow imperatives at oshb:Jer.4.5 and the hear-the-word summons at oshb:Jer.10.1, carry two different shapes. The shape standing at 29:20 is its own count object - the plural hear-the-word-of-YHWH summons with a vocative - and it stands in 10 verses book-wide (sweep: 10 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys: Jer.2.4, Jer.7.2, Jer.17.20, Jer.19.3, Jer.21.11, Jer.29.20, Jer.31.10, Jer.42.15, Jer.44.24, Jer.44.26). All ten were read verse by verse: in every one the summons stands BEFORE the word it announces, and in two of them - oshb:Jer.19.3 and oshb:Jer.42.15, both members of the 32-verse full-stack signature (sweep: 32 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys) - the element the summons introduces stands inside the SAME verse, and it is the koh-amar full-stack title: יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (quoted at byte tier from oshb:Jer.29.21; the recurrence at those two sites is skeleton tier). At 29:20-29:21 that same two-part construction is split across a verse boundary instead: כֹּֽה אָמַר֩ יְהוָ֨ה צְבָא֜וֹת אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte) stands verse-initially in the very next verse. The summons is cataphoric, so it belongs forward with the oracle it announces, not backward as a closing flourish. Cross-seam cohesion runs the same way: the second-person plural address opened at 29:20 is sustained inside 29:21 at הַֽנִּבְּאִ֥ים לָכֶ֛ם בִּשְׁמִ֖י שָׁ֑קֶר and verse-finally at וְהִכָּ֖ם לְעֵינֵיכֶֽם (oshb:Jer.29.21, byte for each) - a byte-true device straddling the CURRENT 29:20|29:21 seam, disclosed by neither row, and under the cohesion rule it argues continuity against that seam. The koh-amar at 29:21 is not an independent cutting onset: the ruled class is a koh-amar onset WITH a frame-owner change, and no frame owner changes there - the same divine mouth inside Jeremiah's letter already carries כִּי כֹ֣ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֗ה (oshb:Jer.29.16, byte) and כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.29.17, byte), and the letter frame is unbroken across all of it. Closure corroboration sits where the moved seam needs it: oshb:Jer.29.19 carries the closure formula twice, נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה and verse-finally וְלֹ֥א שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (byte for each), and neum-YHWH closes a unit only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows - one does, at 29:20. Parashah layer, tier-3 WEAK and single-witness WLC, driving nothing: SAMEKH keyed at MT 29:15, MT 29:20 and MT 29:23, nothing keyed at MT 29:19 (a true absence, stated as non-corroboration only; absence is never counterevidence). The MT 29:20 mark corroborates the seam being moved away from, at tier-3 alone, and under the owner addendum a tier-3-only ground cannot hold a seam against tier-1 text signals. Disclosure-level consistency note, not a driver: after the move each row opens on a marked verse (MT 29:15 and MT 29:20), one reading of the layer applied to both, where the current pair reads the two marks in opposite directions - the asymmetry the challenge upheld.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED SPAN SET. (1) P10-012: Jer.29.15-Jer.29.20 becomes Jer.29.15-Jer.29.19; unit_type judgment_oracle unchanged; parent_collection M6 Jer.25.1-Jer.29.32 unchanged; chunk_index_in_book 136 unchanged; literature_type_guess stands. (2) P10-013: Jer.29.21-Jer.29.23 becomes Jer.29.20-Jer.29.23; unit_type judgment_oracle unchanged (the operative category is still the judgment on the two named false prophets, now opened by its summons); parent_collection M6 Jer.25.1-Jer.29.32 unchanged; chunk_index_in_book 137 unchanged; literature_type_guess stands. (3) No retirement, no new row, no reindexing. TILING: P10-011 still closes at Jer.29.14 and P10-014 still opens at Jer.29.24, both untouched; the pair still tiles Jer.29.15-Jer.29.23 with no gap and no overlap (5 + 4 verses against the previous 6 + 3); 1364/1364 survives; neither row straddles a frame seam - both stay wholly inside M6. SEAM-PAIR CURE - ONE edit installed on BOTH rows, identical claim, no divergent wording: the moved seam is argued once from the cataphoric summons at oshb:Jer.29.20 spliced at byte tier with its object and digit, the doubled verse-final closure formula at oshb:Jer.29.19, and the sustained second-person plural address inside oshb:Jer.29.21 named as the reason the 29:20|29:21 juncture is declined. P10-012 carries it at its back seam; P10-013 carries it at its front seam. DEPENDENT FIELDS re-open on both rows with the driver swap: boundary_rationale, strongest_rejected_alternative, observed_substrate_signals, confidence. P10-012 oss: keep narrative_frame.addressee_shift_report and speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh; add a closure key for the doubled formula now carrying its back seam (divine_title.neum_yhwh_closure). P10-013 oss: add a discourse-imperative onset key under the dotted taxonomy (e.g. narrative_frame.discourse_imperative_summons) as the row's new front-seam driver, add letter_frame.embedded_content as the docket already orders, and keep speech_formula.koh_amar_yhwh_tsevaot_elohei_yisrael, which is now an internal formula rather than the front-seam warrant; parashah.* keys stay barred from oss. P10-012 strongest_rejected_alternative: sentence one keeps the undecided 29:14|29:15 attachment, which this ruling does NOT decide - the row stays at medium_low with its frontier flag; sentence two carries the mandated rival disclosure, the seam-pair cure text. P10-013 strongest_rejected_alternative: the declined 29:20|29:21 juncture, stated with the test that killed it - any retained seam there must cite a tier-1 signal standing in oshb:Jer.29.21's own bytes other than a koh-amar without a frame-owner change, and must say why the sustained second-person plural address does not argue continuity; the verse-22 curse-formula split may stand only as the optional second sentence. P10-013 confidence stays medium. BOUNDARY_EVIDENCE_REFS re-derived on both rows against the new spans (mirror rule): oshb:Jer.29.20 enters P10-012's list as the next unit's onset, and oshb:Jer.29.19 enters P10-013's list as the preceding closure; refs no longer argued come out. DEVICE_NOTES - the mark-disclosure symmetry is a SWEEP over each NEW span, not a spot fix. P10-012 (MT 29:15-29:19): SAMEKH at MT 29:15; paseq segs at MT 29:16 and MT 29:18 (single-witness, count-only, no intra-verse position); the ketiv/qere note at MT 29:18; no mark keyed at MT 29:19. The docket's direction-disclosure order survives, re-pointed: the MT 29:15 seg is stated under one declared direction convention, and this row's own close carries no seg. P10-013 (MT 29:20-29:23): the SAMEKH at MT 29:20 now sits INSIDE the span at its own opening verse and is disclosed there - single-witness, tier-3 weak - and disclosed as corroborating the declined juncture rather than the adopted one; paseq seg at MT 29:21; SAMEKH closing at MT 29:23; the ketiv/qere note and the separate OSHB exegesis note at MT 29:23 (single-witness apparatus, not text bytes). DOCKET ORDERS ABSORBED by this adoption: on P10-012, the order to weigh the 29:19/29:20 juncture in strongest_rejected_alternative (that juncture is now the row's own seam); on P10-013, the order to weigh the summons at 29:20 as a rival onset (it is now the row's own onset). DOCKET ORDERS SURVIVING, executed against the NEW spans: name the tsevaot-headed formula at oshb:Jer.29.17 as its own count object (now inside P10-012); splice the pointed formula at oshb:Jer.29.21 at byte tier at the site where it is argued and name whose mouth carries it and the written medium it stands inside; disclose both attested spellings of the name at oshb:Jer.29.21 and oshb:Jer.29.22 with a per-spelling digit; add the letter-frame key to oss; add every undisclosed seg named above. NOT DECIDED HERE: the 29:14|29:15 attachment, which stays open at medium_low, and no other seam in the chapter.

rulings.docket_item: Resolve the peer's conditional at Jer.30.8: either the row's rejection of the 30:8 cut re-grounds on bytes (no respan) or the cut is ruled adopt/decline.
rulings.grounds: The condition resolves in favour of re-grounding: the rejection can be re-argued on bytes, so the alternative does not become an adopted respan. The refuted half of the row's sentence is confirmed - oshb:Jer.30.8 carries the span's first second-person singular marking, אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק (byte), and a flat denial of any addressee change at that turn is byte-false and may not stand. But that marking is not a member of any ruled tier-1 internal seam class at that verse, on five byte grounds. First, no koh-amar stands at 30:8: the span's onset formula is כִּי כֹה֙ אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.30.5, byte) and the next is כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.30.12, byte). Second, the shift is not an EXPLICIT addressee shift - no addressee is named at 30:8, and the first vocative in the unit stands two verses later at וְאַתָּ֡ה אַל תִּירָא֩ עַבְדִּ֨י יַעֲקֹ֤ב (oshb:Jer.30.10, byte). Third, the persons are mixed inside the one clause: אֶשְׁבֹּ֤ר עֻלּוֹ֙ מֵעַ֣ל צַוָּארֶ֔ךָ וּמוֹסְרוֹתֶ֖יךָ אֲנַתֵּ֑ק sets a third-person suffix beside second-person singular suffixes, and the same verse closes וְלֹא יַעַבְדוּ ב֥וֹ ע֖וֹד זָרִֽים (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte for each) with a third-person reference. Fourth, the marking is not even sustained from 30:8: oshb:Jer.30.9 reverts to third person, וְעָ֣בְד֔וּ אֵ֖ת יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹֽהֵיהֶ֑ם וְאֵת֙ דָּוִ֣ד (byte), so the person layer oscillates across 30:8-30:11 and is not a boundary-grade addressee signal in this unit. Fifth, the verse's own opening וְהָיָה֩ בַיּ֨וֹם הַה֜וּא (oshb:Jer.30.8, byte) is not a date-formula onset: the ruled date object is the year-header shape, while this day formula stands in 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys: Jer.4.9 and Jer.30.8). The neum-YHWH-tsevaot stack inside 30:8 is closure corroboration only and closes a unit solely where a fresh tier-1 onset follows; none does. Marks are tier-3 weak, single-witness WLC, and drive nothing either way: a paseq seg at MT 30:8, SAMEKH at MT 30:9, PE plus a paseq seg at MT 30:11; nothing is keyed at the span's own front seam MT 30:4 (true absence, non-corroboration only).

consequence.spec: NO RESPAN: Jer.30.5-Jer.30.11 stands; P11-001 and P11-003 are untouched; tiling unchanged; 1364/1364 survives. Both of the docket's work orders on P11-002 stand UNCHANGED and remain the controlling author work: (1) the 30:5 quote-gloss parity repair, gloss extent re-cut to splice extent; (2) the rejection re-argued on grounds the bytes support, naming the second-person singular entry at 30:8, the mixed person marking inside that same clause, and the absence of any fresh speech formula there; and the docket's order to disclose the second-person plural imperative pair at 30:6 or carry it in observed_substrate_signals. CURE ADDED BEYOND THE DOCKET, three parts. (a) The re-argued rejection must also carry the two byte grounds this ruling names and the docket does not: the third-person reversion at oshb:Jer.30.9 and the first vocative standing only at oshb:Jer.30.10 - so that the rewritten sentence, read back against oshb:Jer.30.7 through oshb:Jer.30.11, denies no form standing in those verses. (b) This juncture sits inside the ruled consolation core's open-seam region, so it is held open rather than decided: frontier_flag_considered becomes true, confidence moves to medium_low to match the ruled posture for this range, and the rejected alternative's second sentence - the one sentence permitted for the mandated rival disclosure - names the juncture as one of this range's genuinely open seam questions. (c) The day formula at oshb:Jer.30.8 is disclosed with its own object and digit (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys) so it is never read as a date-formula onset. DEPENDENT FIELDS: the driver does NOT change - the koh-amar onset at oshb:Jer.30.5 remains this row's warrant - so observed_substrate_signals and unit_type do not re-open; only confidence and the frontier flag move, with the disclosure. NOT DECIDED: neither the 30:4|30:5 nor the 30:11|30:12 seam is touched, and no other row is affected.

rulings.docket_item: Resolve the peer's conditional at Jer.31.3: re-ground the rejection on bytes, or rule the proposed cut adopt/decline.
rulings.grounds: The condition resolves in favour of re-grounding, so no respan follows. The refutation stands and is confirmed from the bytes: oshb:Jer.31.2 carries no second-person form anywhere, and oshb:Jer.31.3 opens מֵרָח֕וֹק יְהוָ֖ה נִרְאָ֣ה לִ֑י (byte) - the divine name in the third person beside a first-person singular pronoun - with the feminine-singular address entering only after that clause at וְאַהֲבַ֤ת עוֹלָם֙ אֲהַבְתִּ֔יךְ (byte). The row's assertion of one continuous voice addressed to a figure already established at 31:2 is byte-false and may not stand. The cut nevertheless fails on the class list. The junction 31:2|31:3 falls at the opening clause of 31:3, and that clause carries no member of the ruled tier-1 internal seam classes: no koh-amar - the span's only formula onset is כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.31.2, byte), one verse earlier; no discourse-frame imperative; no date-formula onset; and no vision-report opening - the clause reports an appearing, with no shown symbol and no interpretation dialogue, and it is not the showing shape that opens the figs report (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys: Jer.24.1 and Jer.38.21). Nor is there an explicit addressee shift AT the junction: the feminine-singular address begins two clauses inside the verse, so no verse-boundary seam can rest on it. The consistency test the docket sets is met without contradiction: at oshb:Jer.30.12 the seam's driver is the fresh verse-initial koh-amar כִּ֣י כֹ֥ה אָמַ֛ר יְהוָ֖ה אָנ֣וּשׁ לְשִׁבְרֵ֑ךְ (byte), with the feminine-singular pointing corroborating it, whereas at 31:3 no such formula stands. The same pointing is not being weighed two ways; what differs is the tier-1 formula standing beside it. Marks are tier-3 weak and single-witness WLC and bear on nothing here: SAMEKH at MT 31:1 at the front seam, PE at MT 31:6 at the close, no paseq seg and no ketiv/qere note anywhere inside MT 31:2-31:6; absence is never counterevidence.

consequence.spec: NO RESPAN: Jer.31.2-Jer.31.6 stands; P11-004 and P11-006 are untouched; tiling unchanged; 1364/1364 survives. Both docket work orders stand UNCHANGED: (1) the 31:2 and 31:3 pairs re-cut so gloss extent equals splice extent, including the clause the 31:3 gloss leaves uncovered; (2) the continuity assertion replaced by the bytes - no second-person form in 31:2, and 31:3 opening a third-person report with a first-person singular pronoun before the feminine-singular address begins. CURE ADDED BEYOND THE DOCKET, three parts. (a) The replacement rejection must land on the ground this ruling names: the junction clause itself carries no tier-1 class member, and the feminine-singular address enters mid-verse, so the junction cannot carry a seam - read the rewritten sentence back against oshb:Jer.31.2 and oshb:Jer.31.3 and confirm it denies no form standing there. (b) The refusal to give the feminine-singular pointing onset weight here must be stated in the form this ruling gives it - formula-driven at oshb:Jer.30.12, no formula at oshb:Jer.31.3 - so that it does not contradict the weight the same pointing carries at oshb:Jer.30.12. (c) This juncture sits inside the ruled consolation core's open-seam region and is held open, not decided: frontier_flag_considered becomes true, confidence moves to medium_low, and the rejected alternative's second sentence names the junction as one of this range's genuinely open seam questions. DEPENDENT FIELDS: the driver does NOT change - the koh-amar onset at oshb:Jer.31.2 remains the warrant - so observed_substrate_signals and unit_type do not re-open; only confidence and the frontier flag move with the disclosure. NOT DECIDED: the 31:1 attachment question at this row's front seam is untouched and stays where the neighbouring row holds it.

rulings.docket_item: Whether the seam at oshb:Jer.31.29 should be cut (boundary proposal for adoption, never author work).
rulings.grounds: Re-derived across all four verses of the span plus the verse after it. The person marking is exactly as challenged: first-person divine forms at וְזָרַעְתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte) and שָׁקַ֣דְתִּי (oshb:Jer.31.28, byte); none in the last two verses, which are third person throughout - בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד (oshb:Jer.31.29, byte) and כִּ֛י אִם אִ֥ישׁ בַּעֲוֺנ֖וֹ יָמ֑וּת (oshb:Jer.31.30, byte); first person again at וְכָרַתִּ֗י (oshb:Jer.31.31, byte). The row's stated ground, that the same first-person voice continues, is byte-false and the docket's order to replace it stands. The cut still fails, on the class list rather than on the voice. oshb:Jer.31.29's own bytes carry no koh-amar, no discourse-frame imperative, no date-formula onset and no vision-report opening, and there is no addressee anywhere in oshb:Jer.31.27-oshb:Jer.31.30 for an addressee shift to occur across. Its opening clause is ANAPHORIC: the demonstrative in בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֔ם לֹא יֹאמְר֣וּ ע֔וֹד points back to the days announced by the span's own opening verse, הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.31.27, byte), so under the cross-seam cohesion rule a byte-true device binds the proverb material INTO that announcement instead of opening a fresh one. The book carries the same construction intact elsewhere: the anaphoric days-clause stands in 4 verses book-wide (sweep: 4 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys: Jer.31.29, Jer.33.15, Jer.33.16, Jer.50.20), and at oshb:Jer.33.15 and oshb:Jer.33.16 it stands verse-initially (both read from the verse bytes; the recurrence itself is skeleton tier) in two consecutive verses that sit inside the announcement made one verse earlier by the same incipit at הִנֵּ֛ה יָמִ֥ים בָּאִ֖ים נְאֻם יְהוָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.33.14, byte). A bare person shift is not itself a member of the ruled class list - which is precisely why the cut fails here, and the same must then hold of any replacement warrant offered at the back seam. Marks are tier-3 weak, single-witness WLC: SAMEKH keyed at MT 31:26 and MT 31:30, nothing keyed at MT 31:27, MT 31:28, MT 31:29 or MT 31:31, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note inside the span; the layer neither carries nor blocks this junction, and absence is never counterevidence. NOT DECIDED, and left exactly where the docket left it: whether the days-are-coming incipit is itself a member of the tier-1 class list. The question does not arise at oshb:Jer.31.29, which carries no incipit, so this ruling does not need it and does not answer it.

consequence.spec: NO RESPAN: Jer.31.27-Jer.31.30 stands; P11-011 (Jer.31.26-Jer.31.26) and P11-013 (Jer.31.31-Jer.31.34) are untouched; tiling unchanged; 1364/1364 survives. All four docket work orders stand UNCHANGED: replace the byte-false first-person ground in strongest_rejected_alternative; state the back seam's actual byte warrant in boundary_rationale; give the incipit claim its digit and unit with the tier named and disclose the third chapter-internal site at oshb:Jer.31.38; extend the paired renderings at web:Jer.31.27, web:Jer.31.29 and web:Jer.31.31 to the extent of their splices. CURE ADDED BEYOND THE DOCKET, symmetry arm. The replacement back-seam warrant may NOT rest on the person shift alone: that is the ground ruled insufficient at oshb:Jer.31.29, and the owner addendum's symmetry binds a ruling's replacement exactly as it binds a challenge. The back seam must be stated as the class member that stands at oshb:Jer.31.31 - a fresh announcement opening a new object, NOT anaphoric to days already announced, which is the byte discriminator between the two junctions - with the person shift at oshb:Jer.31.31 and the incipit's recurrence digit carried as corroboration, each with its tier named. The replacement must pass the test that killed the original: read it back across oshb:Jer.31.27 through oshb:Jer.31.31 and confirm it denies no form standing there. The byte-true ground for holding the proverb material with what precedes is the anaphoric days-clause, and it is ONE edit: it may be argued once, in strongest_rejected_alternative, and must not be restated in different words in boundary_rationale. DEPENDENT FIELDS: the front-seam driver does not change, so unit_type stays salvation_oracle and parent_collection stays M7 Jer.30.1-Jer.33.26; observed_substrate_signals re-opens only to the extent the docket already orders (the incipit key carrying its digit and the third site disclosed); confidence stays medium. NOT DECIDED: the 31:30|31:31 seam itself is not moved by this ruling - only the form of its stated warrant is constrained.

rulings.docket_item: Fold Jer.38.21-Jer.38.23 into Jer.38.14-Jer.38.20 as one unit closing at the mark keyed to MT 38:23.
rulings.grounds: The bytes carry the fold. The last speech introduction before the junction is וַיֹּ֥אמֶר יִרְמְיָ֖הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.20, byte). oshb:Jer.38.21 then reads, in its entirety, וְאִם מָאֵ֥ן אַתָּ֖ה לָצֵ֑את זֶ֣ה הַדָּבָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֥ר הִרְאַ֖נִי יְהוָֽה (byte) - nine words, so the account is exhaustive: a waw-conditional protasis with no speech introduction, no vocative, no addressee change, no narrative frame and no dated notice. No member of the ruled tier-1 internal seam classes stands in that verse's own bytes. The showing formula does not carry it either: the verb stands verse-medially there, eighth of the verse's nine words, and in 2 verses book-wide (sweep: 2 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys: Jer.24.1 and Jer.38.21), where at oshb:Jer.24.1 it is the verse's own opening word. The row's own device note already concedes the showing is embedded inside an ongoing address, which withdraws the single warrant offered for the cut. Two byte-true devices straddle the junction and, undisclosed, argue continuity against it. A conditional series on the same exit verb runs אִם יָצֹ֨א תֵצֵ֜א (oshb:Jer.38.17, byte), then וְאִ֣ם לֹֽא תֵצֵ֗א (oshb:Jer.38.18, byte), then the protasis of oshb:Jer.38.21 - across two of the prophet's turns, with the proposed seam falling inside the second of them. And the second-person singular address to the king is continuous across the junction, running from the turn opened at oshb:Jer.38.20 into הִסִּית֜וּךָ וְיָכְל֤וּ לְךָ֙ (oshb:Jer.38.22, byte) and וְאֶת כָּל נָשֶׁ֣יךָ וְאֶת בָּנֶ֗יךָ (oshb:Jer.38.23, byte). N8 is the dated narrative chain, where units cut at scene, participant and date seams and frame plus speech is the default larger unit. None of the three changes at 38:21; the next participant change carrying its own speech introduction is וַיֹּ֨אמֶר צִדְקִיָּ֜הוּ אֶֽל יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ (oshb:Jer.38.24, byte), which is where the merged unit ends and the following row already begins. Marks are tier-3 weak and single-witness WLC: PE keyed at MT 38:19 and MT 38:23 with nothing keyed at MT 38:20 (a true absence, non-corroboration only), SAMEKH at MT 38:16 and MT 38:18, a ketiv/qere note at MT 38:16 and a paseq seg at MT 38:20, and no paseq seg or ketiv/qere note anywhere in MT 38:21-38:23. Nothing in the layer supports a junction at 38:21.

consequence.spec: ADOPTED MERGE. rulings.docket_item: Calibration direction, census direction (a): 1 refute in 216 rulings - true primaries challenge precision, or an under-used refutation bar? Record the direction consequence for the spot wave and postcheck sampling posture.
rulings.grounds: The exemplar was re-derived before being used as the calibration standard, and it verifies at every load-bearing point. oshb:Jer.35.18 opens וּלְבֵ֨ית הָרֵכָבִ֜ים אָמַ֣ר יִרְמְיָ֗הוּ (byte), the verse-initial speaker-and-addressee tag the refutation names; the word-event onset it names at oshb:Jer.35.12 is וַֽיְהִי֙ דְּבַר יְהוָ֔ה אֶֽל (byte) and is a member of the 21-verse shape (sweep: 21 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys); both divine-title citations are members of the 32-verse full-stack signature (sweep: 32 verses, skeleton tier, MT keys - oshb:Jer.35.18 and oshb:Jer.35.19 both members); and the mark accounting matches the inventory exactly - SAMEKH at MT 35:18, PE at MT 35:19, nothing keyed at MT 35:17, and no paseq seg or variant note at MT 35:18-35:19, single-witness WLC at tier-3 weak. Its frame-owner digit names a DIFFERENT object from the full-stack signature - the divine formula in a false prophet's mouth - and keeps the two objects apart, which is itself part of what makes it a model refutation. DIRECTION. The rate alone cannot settle the question, and it should not be read as an under-used bar. The round's corrective load is carried by REFINE (77 of 216), not by refute (1 of 216): a challenge whose stated GROUND fails re-derivation while its TARGET defect is real is ruled refine with the ground replaced - the pattern is visible in this slice, where one entry upholds two arms and refines two more precisely because the challenge's own reasoning did not survive the bytes - and refute is left for the case where the target defect is itself absent. The exemplar has that signature exactly: a challenge citing no byte at all, resting on a category-policy reading, against a row whose bytes carry the operative category. On that reading 1 refute in 216 is CONSISTENT with true challenge precision at the target level and is not evidence of a rubber-stamped round. It is equally not proof of calibration: a bar exercised once cannot be distinguished, from the rate alone, from a bar that is under-used. The direction is therefore recorded as unresolved-by-rate, with a falsification arm assigned to the downstream lanes rather than any adjustment to the round's rulings.

consequence.spec: RECORDED DIRECTION: precision-consistent, under-use NOT demonstrated and NOT excluded; refine is the round's corrective valve and the refute rate is not a calibration signal on its own. NO reweighting of any adjudicated row follows from this record, and no ruling in this round is re-opened by it. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE SPOT WAVE: sample preferentially from the REFINE population (77 rulings), where a work order was installed on a ground the reviewer itself re-derived differently, and test one thing per sampled row - whether the replacement warrant passes the test that killed the original, read back against the row's own span bytes. CONSEQUENCE FOR THE POSTCHECK SAMPLING POSTURE: carry a dedicated falsification arm for this direction question - sample a small number of UPHELD rulings whose challenge grounds cite no byte of their own, the exemplar's signature, and ask whether each should have been refuted. That arm, not the rate, is what settles under-use; its finding is recorded as calibration evidence for the round and never as a re-ruling. BOTH LANES: findings are calibration evidence only; neither lane may re-open an adjudicated row's weight, confidence, or ruling. CENSUS RECORDED AS GIVEN (not re-derived): 216 rulings - 138 uphold, 77 refine, 1 refute, 0 escalate; 215 work orders; 1 refuted; 0 escalations; 1 sample defect; 91 corpus-wide-order candidates consolidated into 8 corpus-wide orders, each carried to execution as its own sweep (E-18).
